rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No stale markers, no fixed retrospectives, no session biography.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body freshness stamps (line 5 'Last verified: 2026-07-26'; line 46 'GA on 2026-02-04'; line 62 'stops working 2026-06-30'; line 114 heading 'as of 2026-08-19') are all legitimate freshness claims, the rule's own exception. But the maintainer block at line 139 carries a pre-existing (not touched by the 6d477099..HEAD diff) paragraph this rule bans near-verbatim: '**Source verification (2026-05-14, subagent fact-check pass):** 22 claims checked ... 1 FAIL (... contradicted "no GUI marketplace" framing - rewritten), 3 DRIFTs (... - all softened), 16 PASS, 1 UNVERIFIED-adjacent (... - left as-is).' 'rewritten' and 'softened' are the rule's own named banned examples ('was softened' is quoted verbatim in the compendium). This is pure journey narration (what was found wrong and changed) with no standing constraint a reader can act on today - it states nothing about the CURRENT text, only that something changed once. It is also now fully superseded: the per-source stamped list two lines below it (lines 142-151, dated 2026-07-26/2026-08-20) re-verifies the same claims in present tense with URLs, which is what the rule's own carve-out (an empirical finding that would otherwise be re-derived) actually protects. Harm: a future maintainer reads a changelog fragment that answers nothing about today's text and has to cross-check the newer block anyway to find out what's actually true now - exactly the session-biography clutter this rule exists to keep out. NOT edited by this judge: a same-day repo rule change (curriculum/CLAUDE.md, 2026-08-23, 'Sibling judges race each other') now requires class judges on a multi-class fan-out to stay read-only and return maintainer-note fixes as findings for the orchestrator to apply after all classes return, rather than self-editing.
